description_full: IHS Holding Limited, together with its subsidiaries, develops, owns, and operates shared communications infrastructure in Nigeria, Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, South Africa, and Zambia. The company offers colocation and lease amendment services, which allows customers to lease space on existing towers alongside current tenants, install additional equipment on a tower, and request for ancillary services; build-to-suit sites; in-building solutions and distributed antenna systems, which allows customers to lease space in secure locations within large building complexes, such as shopping malls, stadiums, and airports; non-intrusive small cell installation services on commercial premises, lampposts, and poles; fiber-to-the-tower connectivity services; rural telephony services; and managed services, including maintenance, security, and power supply services. It serves communication service providers, mobile network operators, internet service providers, broadcasters, security functions, and private corporations. IHS Holding Limited was founded in 2001 and is based in London, the United Kingdom.

financial_summary: IHS Holding Limited is a mid-cap real estate business with a $2.8B market cap on $1.6B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -7% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are expanding by +6.8pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 17% against a 10% cost of capital, a 7-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $719M in free cash flow — roughly 45 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 7.38× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -18.0% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.5× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 2.3× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 38% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
